itens.titulo: US Treasury auction changes loom in 2027; dealers eye long-end cuts
itens.descricao: US Treasury auction changes loom in 2027; dealers eye long-end cuts Yahoo Finance
trechos: Primary dealers broadly expect that the Treasury will at some point next year cut auction sizes of 20-year and 30-year bonds while boosting issuance of 2-year to 10-year maturities to offset the funding gap created by reduced long-dated borrowing.
The refunding outlines government financing plans for the fourth quarter and the first three months of 2027, including auction sizes for 3-year and 10-year notes as well as 30-year bonds.

"Expectations have been built up that the US Treasury might foreshadow some changes at this refunding announcement, particularly cuts to the long-end auction sizes," said Guneet Dhingra, head of US rates strategy at BNP Paribas in New York.
"Keep in mind, the Treasury has said they'll be holding coupon sizes steady for the next several quarters.
So anything that actually changes is going to be after the next several quarters, which probably means nothing before August 2027 at the earliest," Dhingra said.

The case for changes to coupon auction sizes strengthened after the Treasury asked primary dealers in a questionnaire what "future changes to auction sizes" should be considered given expected borrowing needs and investor demand.

Speculation that the Treasury could trim issuance of 20-year and 30-year bonds has grown in recent weeks, reflecting expectations that policymakers may look for ways to slow the climb in long-term yields.
The Treasury has already increased buybacks of debt maturing in the 10- to 20-year sector to as much as $6 billion, yet yields have remained stubbornly elevated.

itens.titulo: Bitmine Buys More Ethereum as Tom Lee Calls the Binance Hack Bullish
itens.descricao: Bitmine Buys More Ethereum as Tom Lee Calls the Binance Hack Bullish Yahoo Finance
trechos: Bitmine Immersion Technologies kept its weekly Ethereum buying streak intact, adding 8,573 ETH worth roughly $19 million, while chairman Tom Lee used the record Binance hack to argue that crypto has grown more resilient, not more fragile.
The NYSE-listed company said Monday its holdings now total 6,060,506 ETH, worth roughly $13.7 billion at a reference price of $2,261 per coin.

That represents 4.9% of Ethereum's 122.2 million token supply, leaving Bitmine, by its own count, 99% of the way to its goal of owning 5% of the network, a target it brands the "Alchemy of 5%," reached in just 15 months.
The firm has bought Ethereum every week since launching its treasury strategy on June 30, 2025.
Most of Lee's commentary focused on last week's roughly $6.4 billion theft from Binance, which the FBI has attributed to North Korea.

1, including 216 Bitcoin, $498 million in cash and marketable securities, a $180 million stake in Beast Industries and an $82 million position in Eightco Holdings, which it bills as a rare public proxy for indirect OpenAI exposure.
Bitmine remains the world's largest Ethereum treasury and the second-largest crypto treasury overall, trailing only Michael Saylor's Strategy, which the release said holds about 848,517 BTC.
Strategy recently resumed its own Bitcoin buying with a $66 million purchase after a brief pause.

itens.titulo: Intel Gets Price Target Revamp but Keeps One Major Catalyst
itens.descricao: Intel Gets Price Target Revamp but Keeps One Major Catalyst Yahoo Finance
trechos: Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) remains under pressure after GF Securities cut its price target to $120 from $150, citing the chipmaker's weaker-than-expected fourth-quarter outlook.
Shares fell nearly 1% in premarket trading Monday, extending the pressure after Intel's sharp post-earnings selloff.
GuruFocus has detected 5 Warning Signs with INTC.
Intel guided for fourth-quarter revenue of $15 billion to $16 billion, below Wall Street expectations of roughly $17 billion, while gross margin guidance also weakened.
Management has additionally warned that softness in the PC market could continue into the first half of 2027.
But progress in areas such as advanced packaging and the company's 18A manufacturing process continues to give investors something to watch beyond the immediate weakness in PCs.
The company said data-center demand remains strong and could continue beyond Q4, while client demand is expected to worsen.
For investors, the key things to watch are 18A execution, external foundry customer announcements, data-center supply, PC demand, gross margins and free cash flow.

itens.titulo: AMD Just Dropped 16% in a Month. Is It Time to Sell, or Load Up?
itens.descricao: AMD Just Dropped 16% in a Month. Is It Time to Sell, or Load Up? Yahoo Finance
trechos: Key Takeaways - Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) declined 16% in the month through October 23, while Intel (INTC) fell 29% and the Nasdaq 100 lost 5%, as investors questioned the sustainability of AI infrastructure spending.
- AMD dropped 10.9% on October 30, closing near $505 after Intel's disappointing outlook intensified concerns about semiconductor demand.

- TIKR's October 21 consensus estimates projected AMD's normalized earnings per share to rise from approximately $8 in 2026 to $16 in 2027, supported by expected growth in AI accelerators and data center infrastructure.
- AMD traded at approximately 46x forward earnings as of October 22, above its five-year average of 35x, making the decline a potential long-term buying opportunity rather than an outright bargain.

Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) stock fell 16% in the month through October 23, closing around $517 as concerns about AI infrastructure financing and elevated semiconductor valuations weighed on investor sentiment.

The decline was smaller than Intel (INTC) stock's 29% drop and considerably worse than the Nasdaq 100's 5% pullback, highlighting growing uncertainty over whether AI infrastructure spending could support chipmakers' valuations.

Concerns intensified on October 8 after a Financial Times report indicated that OpenAI's annualized revenue was approaching $50 billion, approximately $20 billion below figures previously circulating in the market.
Further pressure emerged on October 14 when weakness in CoreWeave's bonds intensified concerns about financing expensive data centers.
